clue.text: Coteries may be classified thus

indicators.note: letters that may be classified are sorted into a new order, so the word Coteries is rearranged

explanation.surface: Exclusive little social circles may well be described as secretive and select.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be classified' sorts the letters of COTERIES into a new order; read as a whole, the clue also says that cliques are secret and select.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, which is what a clique keeps to itself.

clue.text: Part of group comprising government employees

indicators.note: comprising means containing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men are US government agents, from FBI slang

explanation.surface: A section of a team is made up of civil servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprising' is the container signal. G-men is American slang for FBI agents; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one part or section of a whole.

clue.text: How rent is paid, correct in every detail

definitions.meaning: rent goes ... in the sense of the one who lets the property, the landlord

explanation.surface: A tenant says the rent is paid exactly as required.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely, and a letter is jokingly also one who lets out property.

clue.text: English turn up and fasten rope

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to veer is to turn

explanation.surface: A sailor from England turns up and ties off a line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the whole run that comes before it; 'and' is a link. Reeve is a sailing term.
explanation.definitionFit: To reeve is a nautical term for threading a rope through a block or ring to secure it.

clue.text: Cold on heath at first, somewhat put shack up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
O, a common short form for on in cricket's leg side

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a bit means somewhat

explanation.surface: A couple out on a cold heath move in together in a makeshift hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link word; 'shack' looks like a hut but 'shack up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shack up is slang for living together as a couple, which is what cohabiting means.

clue.text: Chromosomes — good one is returned to me

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the word for one is read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself, one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geneticist remarks that a fine set of chromosomes has come back to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is returned' is the reversal signal; 'to' only joins. The dash in the surface separates the definition from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A genome is the complete set of an organism's genetic material, carried on its chromosomes.

clue.text: Lord goes to sea, consumed by ambition for first prize

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so these pieces go inside the word for ambition

parts.note: a goal is an ambition
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A nobleman goes to sea, driven by a hunger to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' is the container signal; 'goes to' and 'for' are links. The surface's lord at sea is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The gold medal is awarded for first place in a contest such as the Olympics.

clue.text: Primarily, Nippon's own, home-grown drama

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: Japan's own traditional theatre is homegrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama, so the surface describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is a traditional form of Japanese drama with masks, music and dance.

clue.text: Colourful battle

definitions.meaning: the Battle of ... (1859) in northern Italy, after which the dye was named

explanation.surface: A vivid fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright crimson dye was named after the 1859 Battle of Magenta, fought soon after its discovery.

clue.text: Managed to cut corner after puncture, and to do it completely

indicators.note: the word for corner is placed after the word for puncture

parts.note: managed to do something is got to do it, so got
to hew is to cut, as with an axe
a puncture is a hole
to hog something is to corner it for yourself, as with hogging the road

explanation.surface: A driver with a flat tyre still managed to take the bend and finish the journey regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' fixes the order of the last two pieces; 'to' and 'and' are links. The surface reads 'corner' as a bend in the road, but it is a verb meaning monopolise.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something thoroughly, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Hard part, first part of exam

parts.note: to part things is to sever them

indicators.note: the first part of a word here is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A student complains that the opening section of a test was tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and hard both describe something harsh or demanding, as a severe or hard winter.

clue.text: Recurrent problem person admits is puzzling

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a being is a person or creature

indicators.note: recurrent read as running back, so the word for problem is turned backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone troubled by a recurring difficulty finds it baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurrent' is the reversal signal and 'admits' the container signal; 'is' is a link. Recurrent problem suggests a nagging worry, not arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemusing things confuse or bewilder, which is what puzzling things do.

clue.text: Be born, or be born again

definitions.meaning: to ... of day, come into the world
to undergo a conversion or sudden realisation

explanation.surface: Come into the world, or convert.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both entering the world and having a religious conversion.

clue.text: Go to university, troubled internally, and weakened

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the word for go to

parts.note: to go to a place regularly is to attend it
ate means troubled or worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A student went to university, suffered inner turmoil and was worn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internally' is the container signal; 'troubled' looks like an adjective for the student but supplies a word meaning worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenuated means thinned or reduced in strength, so weakened.

clue.text: Hull's watertightness sampled in lake

indicators.note: sampled says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ship's hull is tested for leaks out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullswater is a lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullswater is one of the largest lakes in the English Lake District, so an example of a lake.

clue.text: Hairy man fusing two metals

parts.note: Es is the chemical symbol for einsteinium, a metallic element
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A shaggy fellow works as a smith, welding two metals together.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Esau is the hairy twin brother of Jacob; 'fusing' simply joins the two symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis describes Esau, elder twin of Jacob, as a hairy man, the classic crossword clue for him.

clue.text: Emend proclamation Conservative has issued

indicators.note: something issued has gone out, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: A Tory government has put out a decree that needs correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has issued' sends the C out of EDICT. The surface reads it as the Conservatives publishing the decree.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct or revise it, which is to emend it.

clue.text: See, ice does melt

indicators.note: melting changes shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Look, the ice really does thaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look, but a see is a bishop's area.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district under a bishop's authority, also called a diocese.

clue.text: Occupation of busy-sounding mobster

indicators.note: sounding says the word for busy is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: busy and lively both describe something full of activity
a hood is a gangster, short for hoodlum

explanation.surface: The clue asks what a gangster who sounds busy does for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: '-sounding' means the first part only sounds like LIVELY; the answer spells it LIVELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A livelihood is the means by which one earns a living, an occupation.

clue.text: Japan to disappear, resistance being suppressed

indicators.note: suppressed means held down inside, so this letter goes within the word

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Japan's resistance movement is being crushed until it vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like the country, but japan is a hard glossy lacquer. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is a black glossy lacquer, so a type of varnish; as verbs both mean to coat.

clue.text: Second, perhaps, in exam interrupted by noise

indicators.note: the word for exam is broken into by another piece

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A candidate's spoken test is disrupted by noise for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a moment of time, but it is an example of a number giving position; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Second is an example of an ordinal number, one showing position in a sequence.

clue.text: Retired man (one of eight, possibly) who has ignored advice of Polonius

definitions.text: who has ignored advice of Polonius

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Rob is a man's name, used here for a man
a rower may be one of the eight in a racing boat

explanation.surface: A pensioner who once rowed in an eight has disregarded some famous fatherly counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Polonius advises 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'. 'Retired' turns ROB into BOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius told his son never to borrow, so anyone who borrows has ignored that advice.

clue.text: Mention retrospectively internal tissue suffering minute loss

indicators.note: looking back, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
suffering loss together signal that a letter is taken away
loss means the letter for minute goes missing

parts.note: the medulla is the inner tissue of an organ such as the kidney

explanation.surface: A doctor refers back to an inner tissue that has been slightly damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDULLA without M gives EDULLA, and 'retrospectively' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to mention it, usually in passing.

clue.text: A short break is over, followed by a farewell

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: hol is a short form of holiday, a break
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brief holiday has ended, and a goodbye follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns HOL into LOH; 'followed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used both for hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Synthesiser extremely exciting to the ear, say

parts.note: electric can mean thrilling, as an electric atmosphere
the ear is an example of an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A music fan says a keyboard sounds thrilling to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the ear' looks like part of the praise of the sound, but 'the ear, say' is an example of a body organ; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthesiser is an electronic keyboard instrument, a kind of powered organ.

clue.text: Encourage, say, the opening of gallery

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Praise, for example, the opening night of an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like a gallery launch, but it picks the G of gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or encourage them.

clue.text: Exhaust resources of 24 in a saloon

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a saloon is a bar
the answer to 24 down, a word for encourage

explanation.surface: Someone drinks away all their money in a saloon.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' refers to the answer of 24 down; 'in' is the container signal and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To beggar someone is to make them poor, using up all their means.

clue.text: Early hit revamped thoroughly

indicators.note: something revamped is renovated or reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old hit song has been given a complete makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something heartily means doing it with full vigour, which is doing it thoroughly.
